name: Alexei Gross
life: “I still remember canceling my own support on the wrong Thursday.” On Wednesday, near Maré Coffee, Alexei likes the table where people coming off shift stop checking the time.
voice: I forgot to cancel because my treatment date moved. I want a calendar with room for uncertainty.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a charcoal zip cardigan and a little coil of soft measuring tape. Alexei has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek, with a thin scattering of white hair over the crown. Alexei raises one eyebrow long before saying yes during a conversation.
personality: Alexei always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Alexei is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To build uncertainty into the care calendar.
family: Bailey Salcedo is Alexei’s younger cousin. Alexei checks the date twice. Bailey brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *Two birthdays in one ward*, Bailey says, “I bought matching cakes before asking either patient which flavors they eat.”
connections: Alan Ko. A canceled treatment and the overseas calendar explain the duplicated appointment.

reactions.response: Alexei asks the client which ordinary task would be easier with two people present.
